staged_now.researcher_notes: The seed source (GASCO's 2024 'National Natural Gas Grid Expansion Projects' deck; the live URL 404s, recovered via a Wayback snapshot with a URL-encoded filename) names this project 'Duplication of the Trans-Sinai pipeline' -- 28 km, 36in, project location 'Sinai' (governorate field, singular), cost 631 million EGP / USD 13,000,000, status 'Under Study'. The cost figure (USD 13,000,000) matches the sheet's ProjectLevelCost exactly, confirming this is unambiguously the right GASCO line item for P8055. But GASCO names no towns or stations -- it is explicitly a DUPLICATION (a parallel/looped second pipe) of an EXISTING Trans-Sinai trunk, not a description of a new, independent corridor. That existing trunk is a 36in, ~196 km line, per EGAS's own 2018 Annual Report, which lists (under pipelines needing rehabilitation) a 'Project Rehabilitation gas supply pipeline Trans-Sinai Pipeline 36"-196 km' with no route detail given either. A related, better-documented project -- GASCO's Abr Sinai Onshore Gas Pipeline EIA (a separate, 111 km line, El-Tina East to El-Arish, cited in the brief) -- describes its own route running parallel to 'the existed Abr Sinai old pipeline' and to 'an existed pipeline' along the El-Qantara-El-Areish desert road, crossing the El-Sheikh Gaber Canal near El-Qantara. This is circumstantial support that the broader 'Trans-Sinai' trunk corridor runs roughly El-Qantara (Suez Canal / Ismailia Governorate side) eastward to El-Arish -- but nothing in any source I could reach names which specific 28 km stretch of that ~196 km corridor GASCO is duplicating, so I have NOT picked coordinates for either end. Given the diameter/cost match is exact but the two named administrative units in GEM's own StartState/EndState ('Sinia' / 'Suez') don't line up with GASCO's single-governorate 'Sinai' location field, I would guess (without evidence) that the duplicated stretch is near the WESTERN, Suez-Canal-crossing end of the trunk (i.e. near El-Qantara) rather than the El-Arish end, since that is the only plausible reading that could produce a 'Suez'-adjacent terminus -- but this is a guess I am explicitly NOT turning into coordinates. FLAG: name-misread: GEM's PipelineName 'Trans-Sinai Gas pipeline II' / OtherEnglishNames 'Trans Gulf Gas PipelineII' does not match GASCO's own name for this project ('Duplication of the Trans-Sinai pipeline') -- it is a parallel/looped segment of an EXISTING trunk, not a second independent 'Trans-Sinai II' line, and I found no evidence it crosses the Gulf of Suez or the Suez Canal shipping lane (the brief's own instinct that a 'Trans Gulf' name is suspicious for a 28km/36in Sinai land-side duplication project appears correct). 'Trans Gulf' does not appear in the source and looks like either a mistranslation or a researcher-invented name.  FLAG: false-lineage-P8013: GEM already has P8013 'Trans Sinia Gas Pipeline I' in the sheet -- I checked its row (StartLocation 'Petreco Plant', EndPrefecture 'Ras Baker Transmissin Station', EndState 'Gulf of Suez', 75 km, 12in, operating). That is a DIFFERENT pipeline: 12in vs this project's 36in, a Gulf-of-Suez oil-field-adjacent facility-to-facility line (Petreco/Ras Baker naming reads as oilfield infrastructure) vs. GASCO's national-gas-grid trunk duplication. Naming P8055 the 'II' to P8013's 'I' asserts a lineage the sources don't support -- these look like two unrelated pipelines that happen to both have 'Trans-Sinai' or 'Sinai' in an English gloss of their name. Recommend NOT treating P8013 as a sister/predecessor line when drawing P8055's route.  FLAG: endpoint-mismatch: sheet's EndState/Province is 'Suez' but GASCO's own project-location field for this exact line reads only 'Sinai' (single governorate, no Suez Canal/Gulf-of-Suez governorate given). Could not corroborate a genuine Suez-side terminus from any source reached.
